submittedParameters.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / identity-preserve. Create ONE new independently painted native HD transparent RGBA running frame, minimum1024 square. ICE SWORD GIRL NORTHEAST rear three-quarter, running diagonally away toward upper RIGHT.
Image1 is new HD NE camera, proportion, identity and full-canvas registration anchor; image2 approved bamboo girl's NE action phase ONLY (never outfit, face, green bow or quiver); image3 Ice's legacy512 NE pose/boot appearance ONLY, not an upscale source; image4 definitive identity; image5 bright polished painted style.
Keep image1 head, hair bun, thin right cheek, long brown hair, icy ornaments, white-blue-gold robe, sash and short white boots. Same fixed canvas, crown and head size and visual support ground as image1. Anatomical bob through joints only, no whole-character move, rescale, crop or lowest-pixel grounding. True short chibi limbs, clear knees/ankles below robe, exactly two connected legs. Shoe heel-to-toe axes follow northeast travel as projected by this camera; no turned-out duck feet. Rear soles visible only by natural knee bend, never ankle twisting.
Near anatomical RIGHT shoulder and sleeve always connect to RIGHT hand holding exactly one ice sword. Far anatomical LEFT holds exactly one blue talisman. Never swap props or append a hand. Counter-swing arms opposite same-side legs, clear elbow. Complete sword inside square, may angle up to avoid edge but shoulder-hand phase matters. Hair follows movement gently, not hiding every joint. No background, cast shadow, FX, text, guide, repeated/copy frame, montage, blur or extra ornaments.

SPECIFIC NEW POSE: NE12 RIGHT near leg extends knee and ankle into final forefoot push, toe remains at virtual ground. LEFT far leg reaches forward/down with heel raised above ground. RIGHT sword forward/up, LEFT talisman back. Both boot axes projected toward NE.
Anatomy emphasis: Image1 already has the silver-blue NEAR RIGHT shoulder connected to FORWARD sword sleeve and far LEFT hand with talisman behind. Preserve that exact upper-body arm ownership, with small continuous changes appropriate to this frame; never swap props. Draw new lower limbs so RIGHT NEAR LEG is the one bearing/pushing off ground and LEFT FAR leg swings forward. Do not retain image1 left support leg phase.
